prompt:
I need the front end for Flowwatch District. A utility monitoring service a mid-sized public school district pays for to watch electricity, gas and water use across its buildings and alert facilities staff when something looks wrong.

Who's using it: Owen Delgado, the district's sole energy and sustainability coordinator, responsible for 14 school buildings. He has a facilities engineering background and gets a steady stream of automated alerts, most of which turn out to be harmless. He's checking in from home on Saturday morning, Nov 21, 2026.

What they're doing right now: Thanksgiving break starts Wednesday and buildings will be empty Nov 25–29. Overnight, the water meter at Lincoln Elementary has shown a constant 6 gallons per minute since 2:00 am, with no school activity. That's either a running toilet, an irrigation zone that should have been winterized, or a real leak. Among 22 alerts from the last 48 hours, he needs to decide whether to call the on-call custodian now or wait until Monday. He also needs to dismiss the alerts that are noise (a Friday night basketball game at the high school, a known meter communication dropout) and confirm all 14 buildings are scheduled into heating setback for the break. He also wants to change his alert rules so only overnight water flow and setback failures can reach him by phone over the holiday.

What's in the system at this point: 14 buildings (9 elementary, 3 middle, 2 high schools) with floor area, typical occupied and unoccupied loads, and meters: 14 electric (15-minute interval kWh), 14 natural gas (hourly therms), 16 water (hourly gallons, including 2 irrigation meters). 22 alerts in the past 48 hours, each with building, meter, rule triggered, time, severity, and status (new, acknowledged, dismissed). Alert rules include 'overnight water > 2 gpm for 3 hrs', 'gas use > 130% of baseline', and 'meter offline > 6 hrs'. HVAC setback schedules for the Nov 25–29 break show 12 buildings confirmed and 2 still missing (Garfield Middle, Roosevelt Elementary). On-call contacts: 3 custodial supervisors with phone rotation. Lincoln Elementary has used about 2,900 gallons since 2:00 am.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
